Messages.Author: Dr. Enrique Montaño
Messages.Body:
1. I read a series of articles and i got confused. In a part it seems
to explain something and in another part it seems to be the opposite.
Can you tell me in a simple way if I can use actions cards and
modifiers when I'm bleeding other methuselae in another turn, but not
mine, via Madness Network?

2. Can I use bewitching even if I'm winning in votes, or it is like
stealth?

Thanks,

Enrique

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
On 24 May 2003 20:18:21 -0700, take...@yahoo.com (Dr. Enrique
Montaño) wrote:

>1. Can you tell me in a simple way if I can use actions cards and

>modifiers when I'm bleeding other methuselae in another turn, but not
>mine, via Madness Network?

If you control the minion who is acting, you may play any and all
appropriate action cards and action modifiers.

>2. Can I use bewitching even if I'm winning in votes, or it is like
>stealth?

You may gain votes at any time during the referendum, there are no
restrictions on the number you can gain (besides not repeating action
modifiers or playing more than 1 political card for a vote).

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
The Lasombra wrote:
> On 24 May 2003 20:18:21 -0700, take...@yahoo.com (Dr. Enrique
> Montaño) wrote:
>
>
>>1. Can you tell me in a simple way if I can use actions cards and
>>modifiers when I'm bleeding other methuselae in another turn, but not
>>mine, via Madness Network?
>
> If you control the minion who is acting, you may play any and all
> appropriate action cards and action modifiers.

Correct. Whose turn it is has no bearing on who can play action
cards or action modifiers. The only thing that matters for that is
who controls the acting minion.

In general, if you read "conflicting" things, check the dates of the
articles and use the most recent. If there is only a slight conflict
(one ruling says one thing about one card, a second says something
different about a different card, and the two together can be read
as saying opposite things about a third card, for example, then
bring that to my attention (to ensure that the reversal was intended).

>>2. Can I use bewitching even if I'm winning in votes, or it is like
>>stealth?
>
> You may gain votes at any time during the referendum, there are no
> restrictions on the number you can gain (besides not repeating action
> modifiers or playing more than 1 political card for a vote).

Correct. The only thing "like stealth" in this context is intercept.
